q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of copper tube per kg?
title: Copper tube carbon footprint per kg
short: Most of copper tube's footprint is its metal: multiply the copper cathode, rod or scrap per kg of tube by the supplier's figure, then add melting or extrusion, drawing and annealing energy. Divide the plant's energy by kg of tube dispatched.
audience: Copper tube makers for air conditioning, refrigeration and plumbing

ul: Copper cathode, rod or scrap by weight.
Yield loss from melting, drawing and trimming.
Melting and casting, or buying in hollow billets.

p: Report per kg of tube by type: level wound coils, straight lengths or inner grooved tube. Name the share of recycled copper.

example.title: Worked example: copper tube unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 168,000 / 500,000 = 0.336 kg CO2 per kg
Add copper metal for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
